questions.subtopic: Irrational Numbers and Proof by Contradiction
questions.context: Question Numbers 19 and 20 are Assertion (A) and Reason (R) based questions. Two statements are given, one labelled Assertion (A) and the other labelled Reason (R). Select the correct answer from the options (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :
questions.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** \((\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{5})\) is an irrational number.

**Reason (R) :** Sum of the any two irrational numbers is always irrational.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
